clustering.caption: Cluster discovery and supervised explanation serve different purposes. The source describes user research.
clustering.notes: Spotify recursively reruns UMAP and HDBSCAN on the original data points of a selected cluster. It trains one-versus-all XGBoost models on the original features and resulting cluster labels, then uses SHAP for explanation. This is not a diagram of Discover Weekly.

anomaly.caption: A low absolute count can be normal. The decision depends on the merchant, time and expected interval.
anomaly.notes: The source discloses trend/seasonal/event modeling, quadratic quantile regression on residuals, Spark training and real-time Java scoring. The interval notation is a teaching abstraction. The diagram does not claim that all anomalies are fraud or that an alert identifies a root cause.

sentiment.sourceLabel: Booking.com team / AWS Machine Learning Blog
sentiment.notes: ABSA means aspect-based sentiment analysis. Human annotators mark and link aspect spans and sentiment spans with SageMaker Ground Truth. The runtime box summarizes the task; it does not assert a specific token classifier or transformer architecture. The sample review and its outputs illustrate the task rather than quoting customer data.

integrated.caption: Generic FAQs and customer-specific operations follow different branches. Missing information triggers clarification.
integrated.sourceLabel: BBVA AI Factory: routing and RAG information agent
integrated.notes: Integrated functional reconstruction from BBVA AI Factory’s routing article (13 November 2025) and RAG information-agent article (18 December 2025). The RAG article explicitly documents conversation reformulation, query/FAQ-title embeddings, cosine similarity and FAQ-grounded generation. It also separates general information from customer-specific operations. Payment and balance are examples named in the routing article. No anomaly detector, forecasting model or sentiment classifier is assumed to be inside Blue.
